passages.title: India's Mineral Security and Strategic Resource Diplomacy
passages.text:
India's rapidly growing economy demands secure and diversified access to critical and strategic minerals essential for its clean energy transition, defence manufacturing, and industrial expansion. The country has emerged as a significant global player in mineral production, ranking among the top producers of key minerals including iron ore and aluminium, while simultaneously grappling with import dependence for several critical minerals vital for emerging technologies like electric vehicle batteries.

India's minerals diplomacy has evolved into a comprehensive strategy spanning the entire mineral value chain. This approach encompasses both domestic reforms and international partnerships, with bilateral memoranda and joint ventures established with multiple nations to promote collaborative extraction in third countries, building diversified supply chains that reduce concentration risks.

Domestically, the government has introduced significant legislative amendments to streamline the auctioning process for strategic minerals, ensuring transparent and efficient resource allocation. The revival of domestic smelting and refining capacity has shown promising results, with certain metals recording sharp production increases in recent fiscal years.

India's mineral security strategy is intrinsically linked to its climate commitments, announced at the COP26 Glasgow Summit in November 2021, which require massive deployment of mineral-intensive clean energy technologies.

passages.title: Economic Survey 2025-26 — Key Highlights
passages.text:
The Economic Survey, India's flagship annual economic document, has a rich history dating back to 1950-51 when it was first presented as part of the Union Budget. Over the decades, it evolved into an independent publication, authored under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) and tabled during the Budget Session of Parliament.

The Economic Survey 2025-26 presented a comprehensive assessment of India's economic performance, highlighting the country's resilience as the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year. The First Advance Estimates placed FY26 real GDP growth at 7.4% and GVA growth at 7.3%, while the Survey assessed the economy's structural fundamentals as remaining strong for sustained medium-term performance.

On the demand side, Private Final Consumption Expenditure grew robustly at 7.0%, reaching 61.5% of GDP — the highest since 2012. Rural and urban consumption both contributed, driven by low inflation at a record 1.7%, stable employment, and increased purchasing power. Gross Fixed Capital Formation grew by 7.8%, maintaining its share at 30% of GDP.

India also established its first International Financial Services Centre to attract global capital, while the Survey recommended continued reforms to sustain growth momentum and build economic resilience.

passages.title: The Shaksgam Valley Dispute
passages.text:
The Shaksgam Valley, also known as the Trans-Karakoram Tract, remains one of the most strategically sensitive territorial disputes in South Asia, involving India, Pakistan, and China. The valley is situated in a remote, high-altitude region characterised by rugged mountainous terrain, glaciers, and harsh climatic conditions, lying north of the strategically vital Siachen Glacier.

The dispute traces its origins to the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement, under which Pakistan ceded approximately 5,180 square kilometres of territory to China. India has consistently rejected this agreement as illegal and void, arguing that Pakistan had no legal authority to cede territory that India claims as its own. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has repeatedly reaffirmed India's sovereign claims over the region as an integral part of the country.

The Shaksgam River flows through the valley, eventually merging with a major river system in China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. China currently exercises administrative control over the area, incorporating it within its county-level governance structure in Xinjiang.

The valley is bordered by prominent mountain ranges and holds significance due to its proximity to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and the Karakoram Highway, making it a geopolitical flashpoint at the intersection of three nuclear-armed nations' territorial claims.

passages.title: India's Doping Crisis and Global Anti-Doping Governance
passages.text:
India's persistent struggle with doping violations in sports has become a matter of serious international concern, with the country consistently recording among the highest number of positive cases globally. The World Anti-Doping Agency, the global independent authority combating doping in sports, has documented India's troubling record through its annual reports, revealing hundreds of positive cases across thousands of samples tested.

The violations span multiple sporting disciplines, with strength-based and endurance-based sports particularly affected. Individual cases have involved prominent athletes across track and field, combat sports, and indigenous games, with substances ranging from anabolic agents and SARMs to stimulants and metabolites. Several athletes have faced multi-year bans, provisional suspensions, and forfeiture of records and medals.

The doping crisis carries significant implications for India's sporting diplomacy and hosting ambitions for major international multi-sport events. International sporting bodies closely scrutinise a nation's anti-doping compliance when evaluating hosting bids, making clean sport governance essential for India's global sporting aspirations.

The global anti-doping framework itself emerged from major doping scandals in professional cycling during the late 1990s, which prompted the international sporting community to establish an independent monitoring body funded through a unique equal partnership model between the sporting movement and governments worldwide.

passages.title: India's Indigenous Microprocessor Journey and DHRUV64
passages.text:
India's pursuit of technological sovereignty has gained significant momentum with the indigenous development of advanced microprocessors like DHRUV64. As part of the nation's broader semiconductor mission, this processor represents a shift away from reliance on foreign intellectual property towards a self-sustaining hardware ecosystem. Built upon the open-source RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), DHRUV64 is engineered to prioritize security and customizability, addressing critical needs in strategic sectors such as defense, aerospace, and secure industrial automation.

Unlike traditional commercial processors that operate as "black boxes," indigenous designs offer transparency, ensuring that no hidden backdoors exist — a crucial requirement for national security infrastructure. The architecture focuses on high-performance computing capabilities while maintaining energy efficiency, making it adaptable for various embedded systems and server-grade applications. This initiative is supported by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to foster a fabless design culture within the country. By mastering complex design flows and logical synthesis, India is not only creating hardware but also nurturing a skilled workforce capable of competing globally. DHRUV64 stands as a testament to the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" vision, laying the groundwork for a future where India is a global hub for semiconductor innovation rather than just a consumer.
